result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.ancestors()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get every node that can reach a given node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L36779-L36842){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.ancestors(node) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Ancestors](/assets/graphs/ancestors.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A seven-node DAG flowing left to right, with the query node F outlined. Following arrows backward from F reaches its parent D and, through D, both A and B, shown in the accent color with the edges used. C and E cannot reach F. The card lists A, B, D." width="100%"} In a directed graph, the ancestors of a node are all nodes with a path *to* it: its parents, their parents, and so on up to the roots. In a dependency graph these are everything the node depends on, directly or indirectly; in a citation network, the work it builds on; in a phylogeny, its lineage. The graph does not need to be acyclic. On an undirected graph, every other node in the same connected component counts as an ancestor (and as a descendant). The node itself is not included. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node whose ancestors to find, as an integer ID or a string label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted IDs of the nodes that can reach `node=`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the label does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a small build pipeline, packaging depends on compiling and testing, which in turn depend on fetching the source: ::: {#6365cf25 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["fetch", "compile", "test", "package", "docs"]) .add_edges([ ("fetch", "compile"), ("compile", "test"), ("test", "package"), ("compile", "package"), ("fetch", "docs"), ]) ) [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in graph.ancestors("package")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['fetch', 'compile', 'test'] ``` ::: :::
